facts_of_case: The parties applied for divorce by mutual consent. The Family Court granted the application vide its order dated 17.08.2023. The wife is in appeal challenging the judgment and decree of the Family Court.

legal_principles.principle: A first appeal against a consent decree of divorce is not permissible.
legal_principles.held: Firstly, Mr.Banaji, learned advocate for the respondent, relied upon a division bench judgment of this Court in the case of Jyoti W/o Darshan Nirmal Jain and Daughter of Chandramohan Dayal vs. Darshan Nirmal Jain, reported in 2012 (2) GLH 206.
cited_cases: Jyoti W/o Darshan Nirmal Jain and Daughter of Chandramohan Dayal vs. Darshan Nirmal Jain, reported in 2012 (2) GLH 206
Anshu Malhotra versus Mukesh Malhotra, reported in 2020:DHC:2021- DB in MAT.Application No.(F.C.) No.86 of 2020 dated 03.06.2020

legal_principles.principle: A party who has obtained a consent decree pursuant to a petition under Section 13-B for mutual consent cannot approach this Court by challenging the same on the ground that the same is being filed by misrepresentation or fraud.
legal_principles.held: Since the issue at large before us is whether it is open for a party who has obtained a consent decree pursuant to a petition under Section 13-B for mutual consent can approach this Court by challenging the same on the ground that the same is being filed by misrepresentation or fraud.

outcome.final_order: The delay in filing the appeal was condoned, and the appeal was disposed of today itself.
